pr_title: Allow DrawableCarouselBeatmapSet to check over its difficulty panels' positions
pr_body:
Closes #8390
Closes #8391 

This PR makes it so that the validity of ``DrawableCarouselBeatmap``'s position is checked by their parent ``DrawableCarouselBeatmapSet``. Beatmap's position is considered valid if a) they aren't higher than their parent set panel and b) they aren't lower than their final position in relation to their parent set's panel would be.

Crude drawing of what the logic looks like:
https://i.imgur.com/NVhoLPg.jpg
``■`` is the beatmap set's panel, ``•`` is the difficulty panel, arrows are their expected movement. Blue line is the minimum allowed Y for difficulty panels, orange is the maximum. If any of these are exceeded, they are brought to the line.

issue_context.title: Panels in beatmap carousel don't pop open correctly after deleting some amount of beatmaps
issue_context.body:
Probably related to #8390

**Describe the bug:** 
After you delete many (idk how many) beatmaps, sets start popping open with incorrect vertical positions for their difficulty panels.

Expected result:  difficulty panels should appear right below their parent's set panel

Actual result: difficulty panels appear way below their parent set panel, sometimes inside the next set's set panel

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
Managed to trigger the bug at 1:06 or so https://youtu.be/jVbm1Tvgz0E?t=68

**osu!lazer version:** 
2020.320.1
comments: not specific to deleting, can be randomly triggered otherwise. the issue is just to do with transform decisions (whether to apply or not).

review_comments: If it the beatmap set panels weren't entirely decoupled from the difficulty panels before the introduction of this list, this could have been a `osu.Framework.Caching.Cached` (*not* the DI attribute), but as things stand this list is needed in this current implementation.

I was confused about this when I first read it. The panels actually need to be decoupled and to my knowledge always have been. The logic to remove offscreen panels from the scene graph relies on all the panels being decoupled. Otherwise removing one panel might remove stuff some others rely on. 
So yeah, this can't use caching.
